en: The *Amitābha-dundubhi-svara-rāja-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. Translator unknown;
now appended to the Liang Dynasty records.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Gaṅgā-śīrṣa pool in the great city of Campā, together with...
The great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus was gathered together.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:

"I shall now expound for you: in the western direction there currently exists a world called Sukhāvatī, where a Buddha resides named Amitābha. If there are members of the fourfold assembly who can correctly receive and uphold the name of that Buddha, by virtue of this merit, when they are on the verge of death, Amitābha will come to that person’s side with his great assembly, enabling them to behold him."
Having seen this, they immediately gave rise to joy and gladness, and their merit increased manifold.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, in whatever place they were born, they would forever be free from the defiled forms of the womb and desire; they would dwell purely within fresh and wondrous precious lotus flowers, being spontaneously transformed by birth, endowed with great supernormal powers, and radiant with brilliant light.
"At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all together praised that Land of Peace and Bliss:
'All the Buddha-dharmas are inconceivable;
the manifestation of supernormal powers and various skillful means are inconceivable.'"
"If there are those who can believe in such matters as these, you should know that such persons are inconceivable;
the karmic retribution they obtain is likewise inconceivable.
"Amitābha Buddha, together with his śrāvakas—the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—has a land called Pure Tranquility (Qingtai)."
The city where the Holy King dwells is ten thousand yojanas in length and breadth, and it is filled with the Kṣatriya caste.
The father of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha was the Cakravartin King Candracchattra;
his mother was named Viśeṣacāritra.
His son was named Candraprabha;
his attendant disciple was named Vimalakīrti;
and his wisdom disciple was named Bhadrapāla.
The diligent application of the bases of psychic power is called "Great Transformation.
At that time, there was a Māra named Invincible (Ajita).
There was also a Devadatta named Tranquil (Śānta).
Amitābha Buddha was together with sixty thousand great bhikṣus.

"If there are those who receive and uphold the name of that Buddha, making their minds firm and mindful without forgetting, abandoning distraction for ten days and ten nights, diligently cultivating and accumulating the *nien-fo samādhi* (Buddhānusmṛti-samādhi), knowing that the Tathāgata eternally dwells in the Land of Peace and Bliss, maintaining continuous mindfulness without interruption, and receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting this Great Dhāraṇī of the King of Drum-Sounds; if for ten days and ten nights they focus their minds on him during the six periods of the day and night, prostrating themselves with the five limbs touching the ground to pay homage to that Buddha, then with firm right mindfulness they will completely eliminate all distractions."

If one can maintain the mind without interruption from moment to moment, within ten days one will certainly behold that Amitābha Buddha, as well as the Tathāgatas of the worlds of the ten directions and their respective abodes.

Except for those with heavy karmic obstructions and dull faculties who cannot behold it even in this brief moment, all their various merits shall be dedicated toward the aspiration to be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

On the day of their passing, Amitābha Buddha, together with his great assembly, will appear before that person to offer comfort and praise them as virtuous; at that moment, the person will experience profound joy.
"By these causes and conditions, according to their aspirations, they shall immediately attain rebirth there.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"What is called the Great Dhāraṇī of the King of Drum-Sound?"
"I shall now speak; listen well.
"Yes, we shall receive your instruction.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One spoke this incantation:

*Svāhā* (58). This is the Great Dhāraṇī of the King of Drum-Sound, Amitābha.

If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, they should always, with utmost sincerity, receive, uphold, read, and recite it, practicing according to its instructions and performing this method of upholding.

One should dwell in a secluded and quiet place, bathe the body, wear new and clean garments, consume pure and simple food and drink, refrain from eating alcohol, meat, or the five pungent herbs, and constantly cultivate the pure conduct of a brahmacārin.
With exquisite incense and flowers, one should make offerings to the Tathāgata Amitābha and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas at his place of enlightenment.

One should always thus single-mindedly fix the mind upon him, making a vow to seek rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss. By practicing with diligence and without indolence according to that vow, one will certainly attain rebirth in that Buddha-world.
At that time, Amitābha Buddha sat with the great assembly upon precious lotus flowers. In that land, the groves, flowers, and fruits were in full bloom, interspersed and magnificently adorned.
Furthermore, from the king of trees, fragrant winds, and wafting scents, there issued forth harmonious and elegant sounds, exclusively proclaiming the unsurpassed and inconceivable Dharma.
There was also a wondrous fragrance called "Radiance," as well as various ointments and incenses, all of which were precious perfumes.
"Amitābha Buddha sits cross-legged upon a great precious lotus flower.
There are two bodhisattvas:
one named Avalokiteśvara and the other named Mahāsthāmaprāpta; these two bodhisattvas stand in attendance to his left and right, surrounded on all sides by innumerable bodhisattvas."
Among this assembly, those who can have deep faith and harbor no doubt will certainly attain rebirth in the Land of Amitābha.
There, the ground is of pure gold, and lotus flowers made of the seven treasures spontaneously emerge.
"If there are members of the fourfold assembly who receive, uphold, read, and recite the name of that Buddha, they shall have no fear of water, fire, poison, or weapons;

nor shall they have any fear of yakṣas and the like, except for those with past grave offenses and karmic obstructions. At the very latest, within seven lifetimes, their vows will surely be fulfilled."
When the Buddha had spoken this Dharani of King Amitabha’s Drum-like Voice, immeasurable sentient beings all made vows, aspiring to be born in that world of Ultimate Bliss.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent!
According to your aspiration, you shall certainly be born there."
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, rejoiced and leaped for joy;
they paid homage and reverently put it into practice. *The Amida Drum-Sound King Dhāraṇī Sūtra*.
